5: Eligibility for Reserve Component Survivor Benefits Program (RCSBP) annuity: court held the eight most recently accrued years of qualified service were not in a reserve component, so the claimant was not eligible.
Because Mr. Tillotson's eight most recently accrued years of qualified service were not in a reserve component, Ms. Taylor-Tillotson is not eligible for RCSBP benefits.
215: Military pay and discharge: whether the Board for Correction of Naval Records' denial of record correction and backpay, based on a positive cocaine urinalysis and a finding of knowing, wrongful use, was supported by substantial evidence and not arbitrary or capricious.
Because the Board's decision was supported by substantial evidence and was not arbitrary, capricious, or contrary to law, we reverse.
753: Military pay, discharge, disability retirement: entitlement to military disability retirement after involuntary discharge; ABCMR denial upheld as not arbitrary, capricious or unsupported by substantial evidence.
we perceive no error in either the analysis of the Court of Federal Claims or that of the ABCMR.
1291: Military pay and discharge: Board reasonably denied back pay and upgrade of dishonorable discharge, relying on the court-martial conviction.
The Board reasonably declined to award Mr. Randolph back pay and upgrade his discharge status, relying on his court-martial conviction.
1476: Military pay and restoration to Active Guard Reserve (AGR) status: whether Smith was entitled to restoration rights under ANGI 36-101 §§2.8.3, 7.8.1, 2.2.1.1 and 7.5 after his Naval War College tour; the court held he was not entitled to restoration and the Court of Federal Claims ruling was in accordance with law.
On review of the statute and regulations, and the position of the government, we conclude that the ruling of the Court of Federal Claims is in accordance with law.
2575: Military disability retirement and correction of military record: whether Pillette was entitled to a medical retirement or PEB referral after his 1966 discharge; the court held the Army properly processed him under AR 635-40 and the MEB's fitness finding made PEB referral unnecessary.
Pillette is therefore not entitled to correction of his military record.
3004: Military Pay Act back-pay claim: whether a naval officer confined pre-trial and later convicted is entitled to pay for the confinement period; court held he is not entitled to pay.

In other words, it is clear from a plain reading of the statute and regulations that a service member's absence while in confinement, including pre-trial confinement, is determined based on the outcome of his case.
3095: Military discharge and promotion/continuation-board claim under the Military Pay Act: dismissed because Santana failed to exhaust the mandatory special-board review under 10 U.S.C. 1558 before suing.
We hold only that the Claims Court correctly dismissed Santana's claim for her failure to exhaust applicable administrative remedies.
3274: Military discharge: alleged failure to conduct a medical examination before disenrollment did not violate any applicable statute or regulation
The statute and regulation on which he relies to show entitlement to a medical examination, 10 U.S.C. 2107(j) and DoDI 1215.08, sec. 6.10.1, do not apply to his case.
3275: Military discharge: denial of right to appear before the August 17, 2006 PRB was a due process violation that was not harmless, so the disenrollment was not inevitable and the harmless error holding is reversed

Given the concession by the government that Mr. Kennedy's due process rights had been violated when he was dissuaded from attending his PRB, and its concession that the error was not harmless, it is clear that the Court of Federal Claims erred in concluding that Mr. Kennedy's disenrollment was inevitable
3788: Military pay and discharge claims: 37 U.S.C. 204 pay claim and disability retirement claim held not viable against the government.
4343: Military discharge via selective continuation board: SecAF's instructions violated DoDI 1320.08 by narrowing the protective window and reversing the presumption of continuation; no unusual circumstances identified; special board ordered for Engle.
The Secretary must continue officers within six years of retirement unless there is a reason that overcomes the presumption that he must do so.
4482: Military pay, discharge, disability retirement: whether the Secretary of the Navy properly rejected the records correction board's recommendation to grant six months of service credit for retirement eligibility.

The Secretary acted within his discretion in rejecting the recommendation of the Board. His 2018 rejection decision was supported by substantial evidence and was not arbitrary, capricious, or contrary to the law.
4483: Whether the Secretary's rejection of the board recommendation was supported by substantial evidence, including the claimed 1993 misconduct finding, which the dissent found unsupported and the majority deemed harmless.
No matter the number of early instances of misconduct, the Secretary's rejection decision is supported by substantial evidence.
4963: Military pay: whether Sharpe, reinstated after an unlawful separation, is entitled to the San Diego BAH rate or only the Norfolk rate he received before separation. The court upheld the Navy's award of the Norfolk rate under the constructive service doctrine.
the Navy's decision to place Mr. Sharpe in the same position he was in before his improper separation by paying him the BAH rate for Norfolk was not arbitrary, capricious, or contrary to law.
4964: Military pay: whether Sharpe is entitled to career sea pay and a CSP premium for the period of his separation. The court upheld the Navy's denial because he could not claim to have been assigned to or serving on a ship during constructive service.
On this basis, the Navy's decision to deny him CSP and a CSP premium for that time period was not arbitrary, capricious, or contrary to law.
5004: Military discharge and disability retirement claims time-barred under 28 U.S.C. 2501; unlawful discharge and back pay claims accrued and expired before filing
We agree with the government that the Claims Court correctly dismissed Maxberry's service-related claims as barred by the statute of limitations.
5158: Military disability retirement under 10 U.S.C. 1204: the court held that Pipes was lawfully ordered to perform the SFIP while in duty status during inactive-duty training, so the non-duty-status rationale used by the AFBCMR and Claims Court was erroneous; reversed and remanded to the AFBCMR for further assessment of his request for correction.

Thus, we hold that, to the extent their analysis turned on Pipes' duty status at the time of his orders, both the AFBCMR and the Claims Court erred in concluding that Pipes was not lawfully ordered to perform the SFIP designed for him.
5510: Military disability retirement and discharge-status upgrade: the Board for Correction of Naval Records' denial of disability retirement pay and an upgrade from other-than-honorable discharge was not arbitrary, capricious, contrary to law, or unsupported by substantial evidence.
Because we agree with the Claims Court that the Board's decision was not arbitrary, capricious, contrary to law, or unsupported by substantial evidence, we affirm.
6626: Military pay: Military Pay Act claim dismissed because Waters voluntarily retired and was therefore not eligible for compensation under 37 U.S.C. § 204; the court also found his retirement was not rendered involuntary by his request to the General Counsel.
his request to the General Counsel was insufficient to render involuntary Mr. Waters’s voluntary retirement.
6678: Military disability retirement claim dismissed because no competent military board first considered the claim under 10 U.S.C. § 1201.

The Court of Federal Claims lacked jurisdiction to consider Mr. Evans's claim for military disability retirement benefits because he never submitted an initial request for such benefits to a competent military board.
7101: Whether Prestonback's Form 5-50 educational assistance service agreement rests on a statutory right governed by statutory principles rather than contract law (military pay and benefit entitlements); court held it is statutory, favoring the Government.
The Court of Federal Claims appropriately determined that Mr. Prestonback's agreement with the Army, memorialized through Form 5-50, rests upon a statutory right.
7102: Whether Prestonback voluntarily failed to complete his active duty service under 10 U.S.C. § 2005 when he was involuntarily separated for substandard performance, so that recoupment of educational assistance was authorized; court held he did voluntarily fail, favoring the Government.
we conclude that Mr. Prestonback voluntarily failed to complete his period of active duty for substandard performance.
7142: Military retirement back pay: the court held McCord could not recover additional military retirement back pay for June 2012 to October 2017 because of the 38 U.S.C. § 5304(a)(1) bar on concurrent military retirement pay and VA benefits.
We conclude that McCord is not entitled to receive additional military retirement back pay for the period June 2012–October 2017.
7146: Out-of-pocket medical expenses: the court held McCord proved his damages of $4,760.97 from being excluded from TRICARE coverage and directed an award.
we conclude that McCord has shown his damages and is entitled to an award of $4,760.97.
7574: Military disability retirement: whether the Board for Correction of Naval Records decision denying conversion of honorable discharge to disability retirement under 10 U.S.C. 1201 was supported by substantial evidence
Substantial evidence supports the Board's determination made after remand.
7732: Military disability retirement claim: accrual of claim for disability retirement pay under 10 U.S.C. §1201 at 1988 discharge, barred by six-year statute of limitations
we agree with the government that Mr. Jones's claim accrued in December of 1988.
7832: Military disability retirement: whether the BCNR's denial of disability retirement pay (unfitness due to bipolar disorder at discharge) was supported by substantial evidence and was not arbitrary or capricious.
These findings are supported by substantial evidence—including the medical records discussed in the Advisory Opinion on which the Board relied.
8125: Military disability retirement claim accrual; statute of limitations under 28 U.S.C. § 2501 barred claim because it accrued at discharge in 1999

We hold that the Mr. Pohl's claim for disability retirement rights accrued in 1999, at which time he had actual and constructive knowledge of his § 1204 benefits, and the statutory six-year statute of limitations began to run.
8254: Whether Pinto was automatically promoted to First Lieutenant due to the flag removal or the late DA Form 78, entitling him to back pay and retroactive promotion; held not automatic.
Thus, Mr. Pinto is not entitled to an automatic promotion to First Lieutenant or any of the relief related to promotion to First Lieutenant, including back pay.
8255: Whether the Army erred in involuntarily separating Pinto under AR 600-8-24 ¶ 5-11 rather than the elimination procedures of ¶ 4-2.a.(2) and ¶ 4-4.b.; held the separation was proper.
Therefore, we agree with the trial court that the Army did not procedurally err in separating Mr. Pinto under AR 600-8-24 ¶ 5-11 instead of AR 600-8-24 ¶ 4-2.a.(2).
8329: Military pay, discharge, disability retirement: whether Army removal of a lieutenant colonel at 28 years was proper; court construed 10 U.S.C. §14706(a)(3) and (b) to exclude law-school service, entitling the officer to exclusion.
we reverse the Claims Court's judgment and remand for further proceedings consistent with this opinion.
8330: Construction of 10 U.S.C. §14706(b): whether the exclusion is barred for service preceding student status; court held §14706(b) bars only the period of service preceding the advanced education, not the officer category.
we construe § 14706(b) to provide that the exclusion does not apply to "the period of service preceding the member's service in a student status."
8614: Military correction and discharge: the BCNR and Claims Court applied the wrong standard by failing to give Doyon's petition liberal consideration under the Kurta Memo; vacated and remanded for liberal consideration.
the Kurta Memo requires that the BCNR review Mr. Doyon's application with liberal consideration.
8615: Retroactive application of 10 U.S.C. § 1552(h), enacted after Doyon filed his BCNR application: the court held § 1552(h) applies to the BCNR's decision and that the boards erred by not considering it.
We therefore hold that the BCNR and Claims Court erred by failing to consider the effect of § 1552(h) on Mr. Doyon's application.
8616: Scope of § 1552(h): 'review of a discharge or dismissal' covers challenges to the narrative reason for discharge (not limited to characterization upgrades), and liberal consideration applies to the circumstances resulting in discharge.
the statute also states a second, broader basis for liberal consideration: whether PTSD "potentially contributed to the circumstances resulting in the discharge or dismissal."
8716: Military involuntary retirement: whether the Coast Guard's CRSP involuntary retirements of enlisted members were lawful under 14 U.S.C. § 357(j) 'reduction in force' exception, where positions were not eliminated.

Because the Claims Court correctly concluded that the proper meaning of the term "reduction in force" in 14 U.S.C. § 357(j) does not cover the discharge program for grades E-7 and above at issue here, we affirm the Claims Court's partial final judgment.
8719: Military disability retirement: whether the Army Board for Correction of Military Records had authority to grant disability retirement without correcting the DD-214 under 10 U.S.C. 1552(f); court held correction of DD-214 was not necessary and 1552(f) does not bar it, reversing dismissal.
we hold that the Court of Federal Claims erred in holding that the ABCMR lacked authority to grant the relief Mr. LaBonte is seeking.
9419: Military pay and retirement grade: whether Campbell is entitled to retired pay at the rank of colonel under 10 U.S.C. § 1372 and the Military Pay Act, given he was never promoted or selected for promotion. Court held he was not entitled.
Mr. Campbell falls into neither category.
9421: Military disability pay: whether Campbell is entitled to an increase in his Army permanent disability rating (70% to 75%) based on a later VA rating increase; ABCMR denial upheld as not arbitrary or capricious.
The ABCMR’s decision was not arbitrary, capricious, or otherwise contrary to law.
9496: Military disability retirement: whether the claim accrued at discharge (timeliness under §2501 turned on knowledge of permanent disability) and whether voluntary request for discharge defeats entitlement to disability retirement pay
We reverse the dismissal for untimeliness.
10465: Survivor Benefit Plan spousal consent: whether 10 U.S.C. § 1448 as in force in 1995 required the surviving spouse's consent for a reservist under age sixty to forgo SBP participation. Court held no consent was required, for the government.
Congress's spousal consent requirements did not apply under these circumstances.
10578: Military pay claim under the Military Pay Act: the court held Richardson's retirement was voluntary, so his claim for reinstatement, promotion and back pay failed on the Carmichael involuntariness test.
We begin and end with the third element for rebutting the presumption of voluntariness.
10660: Military disability retirement: the Board for Correction of Naval Records' fitness determination was arbitrary and capricious because it failed to evaluate all SECNAVINST 1850.4E § 3304 criteria; vacated and remanded.

we hold that the Record Correction Board's decision to deny Mr. Kelly's request to correct his military record to reflect military disability retirement pay under 10 U.S.C. § 1201 was arbitrary and capricious and unsupported by substantial evidence.
10772: Whether retired military officers may serve as members of the Board for Correction of Naval Records under 10 U.S.C. § 1552(a)(1), which requires boards of civilians; held retired members qualify as civilians, so the BCNR decision denying correction stands.
Accordingly, we hold that the term "civilians" in 10 U.S.C. § 1552(a)(1) includes former and retired members of the military serving in the civilian arm of the military organization at issue.
10943: Military pay: Hilaire is not entitled to have his non-prior service enlistment bonus paid retroactively into his TSP account because he made no TSP contribution elections during the years the bonus was due (5 C.F.R. § 1605.13(b)(1)).
Consequently, Hilaire is not entitled to retroactive deposits into his TSP account.
10944: Military pay: the maximum non-prior service enlistment bonus Hilaire can receive is $8000, based on his August 31, 2005 enlistment date, not the $15,000 maximum he claimed.
Based on the statute and regulation in effect on Hilaire's enlistment date, he is eligible for a NPS enlistment bonus no greater than $8000.
11555: Army administrative separation of a service member under other than honorable conditions based on commission of a serious offense (Army Reg. 635-200 ¶ 14-12c); court held the assault and stalking offenses supported the discharge and affirmed judgment for the government.
Thus, Mr. Horton's assault and stalking offenses support his discharge under ¶ 14-12c.
11630: Military pay claim under 37 U.S.C. § 204: whether the Navy retirement was voluntary, so the separated plaintiff failed to state a claim; dismissal affirmed.
Thus, Commander Frank has failed to plausibly plead that she involuntarily accepted the terms of the government.
12166: Military disability retirement: whether Pipes was in inactive-duty training duty status when injured, which turned on whether the AFMAN's advance-authorization requirement applied to all IDT and whether the lawful order to participate in the SFIP itself authorized IDT status. Court affirmed the government's denial.
We cannot say that this finding is arbitrary, capricious, contrary to law, or unsupported by substantial evidence.
12842: Military discharge under the Military Pay Act: the Corrections Board's determination that Osburn was properly separated for false official statements (Article 107) was supported by substantial evidence and was not arbitrary or capricious, so the Claims Court's judgment for the government was affirmed.
We conclude the Corrections Board's determination was not erroneous and that the Claims Court's decision should be affirmed.
13068: Combat Related Special Compensation calculated at the VA disability rating (50%) rather than the Army's 70% rating; claimant not entitled to 70% calculation.
Because Mr. Hutchinson does not dispute that his VA rating for PTSD is 50%, he was not entitled to a calculation at the 70% rate.
13069: Eligibility for Concurrent Retirement and Disability Pay; servicemember retired for permanent disability with less than 20 years of service is ineligible under 10 U.S.C. § 1414(b)(2).

The statute authorizing Concurrent Retirement and Disability Pay expressly provides that servicemembers retired due to permanent disability with less than 20 years of service are ineligible for Concurrent Retirement and Disability Pay.
13070: Backdating retirement benefits at the rank of Major before the President signed the promotion; no authority to retroactively promote.

He is not eligible for benefits at the rank of Major before the date his promotion was signed by the President, and we lack the authority to retroactively promote him to a rank for which he had not previously been duly appointed.
13071: Entitlement to further retroactive promotion and benefits under 10 U.S.C. § 1372; no record showing actual and lawful promotion to a higher rank.

Mr. Hutchinson fails to identify any support in the record for the proposition that he was actually and lawfully promoted to any higher position, a requirement for receipt of benefits at a higher rank.
13084: Military retirement grade: whether Col. Bader was properly retired at the rank of Colonel rather than Brigadier General, which affected his retirement pay under 10 U.S.C. § 1370 and the AFBCMR's determination that his service at Brigadier General was unsatisfactory due to ethics violations.
We agree that the government demonstrated that Col. Bader engaged in serious misconduct and the Claims Court properly granted the government's motion for judgment on the administrative record.
13241: Military retirement grade: whether the record supports the Secretary's finding that the multiple affairs with women at O-7 grade were misconduct warranting retirement at O-6; substantial evidence supported the Board's finding
the SAF/IG report contains substantial evidence to support the Board's finding regarding Mr. Gersten's relationships with multiple women while serving at the grade of O-7.
13450: Military disability retirement fitness determination: Board failed to consider the SECNAVINST 1850.4E 3304 factors (common military tasks, deployability, special qualifications) and the MANMED nuclear field duty standards; fitness determination vacated and remanded.

Thus, we hold that the Board erred under § 3304 by failing to consider Mr. Qoye's common military tasks, deployability, and special qualifications, each of which was arbitrary and capricious and independently warrants vacatur and remand.
13452: Liberal consideration under 10 U.S.C. 1552(h) and the Kurta Memo: Board improperly held that an honorable characterization of service precluded liberal consideration of a discharge narrative change; remanded for the Board to decide whether narcolepsy is an eligible condition.
We agree with Mr. Qoye that the Board's rationale for determining liberal consideration does not apply to his request was improper.
13473: Military disability retirement fitness determination: the BCNR applied the wrong legal standard under SECNAVINST 1850.4E §§ 3301 and 3304 (failure to identify duties of Infantry Unit Leader, and failure to consider common military tasks and deployability).
We conclude that the BCNR legally erred under § 3301.
13474: Liberal consideration under 10 U.S.C. § 1552(h) applies to the BCNR's fitness determination, and the BCNR failed to apply liberal consideration to Mr. Bee's petition.
We hold that the BCNR failed to give Mr. Bee's petition liberal consideration.
13538: Military disability retirement: whether the PDBR's 50% disability rating and refusal to match his 100% VA rating was arbitrary, capricious, or contrary to law under 10 U.S.C. § 1216(a); the court affirmed judgment for the government on the second claim.
The government's arguments in support of the final decision are compelling, and Mr. Rickel's attempt to overcome those arguments is unavailing.
13745: Military pay, discharge, disability retirement: whether Conti has a clear-cut legal entitlement to retroactive promotion to E-7 with back pay under the Military Pay Act; dismissal of complaint affirmed.

Here, we must affirm the dismissal of Ms. Conti's complaint because it does not allege facts supporting an inference of a "clear-cut legal entitlement" to a retroactive promotion from the E-6 grade . . . to the rank and grade of E-7.
13814: Military disability compensation: whether DoD FMR 7B ¶630801.C exempts a veteran with an IU rating from the 10 U.S.C. § 1413a CRSC cap, and whether the Board's denial of CRSC correction was arbitrary or capricious; held the cap applies and the government prevails.
Accordingly, as the Court of Federal Claims rightly held, the Board's decision to deny correction of Mr. Garcia's CRSC pay was not arbitrary and capricious.
13998: Military pay and discharge: whether the Board's finding that the Secretary would have approved release from active duty during the sanctuary period was lawful under 10 U.S.C. 12686(a) and SECNAVINST 1920.6C para. 7(b)(3); the court rejected the service member's reading of the instruction.

In sum, we reject LtCol Faerber's reading of the instruction, and we therefore see no error in the Board's decision based on the asserted lack of authority of the Secretary to have released LtCol Faerber from active duty during his sanctuary period.
13999: Military pay and retirement remedy: whether the constructive service doctrine barred the Board from finding the service member would have been released during the sanctuary period (retroactive release date); the court rejected the challenge.
The Board adhered to the constructive-service doctrine here. Accordingly, we reject LtCol Faerber's challenge on this issue.
14015: Military pay, discharge, disability retirement: Count X accrued leave and time-in-service calculation; ABCMR decision upheld, Buholtz denied pay for leave and bad time.
we will not disturb the decision of the ABCMR because it is not arbitrary, capricious, contrary to law, or unsupported by substantial evidence.
14113: Military disability retirement: whether sinusitis was an unfitting condition preventing performance of Generalist Pilot duties, including whether flying was among the duties; Board decision upheld as supported by substantial evidence.
We conclude that the Board's finding that flying was not part of his duties is supported by substantial evidence, and therefore we conclude that Mr. Henrikson has not identified any reversible error.
14267: Entitlement to a Survivor Benefit Plan annuity under 10 U.S.C. 1448(d): whether the former spouse's failure to make a timely written deemed-election request under 1450(f)(3) defeats her claim so that the surviving spouse is the proper beneficiary
Because Mrs. Bannister is the proper beneficiary of the SBP annuity under the governing statute, we reverse the denial and remand for a determination of the annuity benefits due to Mrs. Bannister.
14300: Military discharge: whether Cunningham was a probationary officer not entitled to a board of inquiry under AR 600-8-24 (three-year appointment rule).
The Court of Federal Claims did not err in finding that Mr. Cunningham was a probationary officer who is not entitled to a hearing by a board of inquiry.
14301: Military discharge: whether the Army's procedural errors in processing the elimination paperwork (failure to consider the original rebuttal) were harmless.

Because the Army came to the same conclusion as its initial recommendation after reviewing Mr. Cunningham's rebuttal statements, any alleged errors in processing Mr. Cunningham's elimination paperwork were harmless.
14302: Military discharge: whether substantial evidence supported the Article 15 finding of wrongful cocaine use under UCMJ Article 112a and AR 27-10 compliance.
There is substantial evidence supporting the conclusion that Mr. Cunningham knowingly ingested cocaine, including the evidence from the urinalysis test.
14799: Military records and back pay: whether the AFBCMR decision upholding the NJP and denying correction was arbitrary, capricious, or unsupported by substantial evidence, including the MWPA reprisal argument.
The AFBCMR’s decision with respect to the NJP was therefore not arbitrary, capricious, contrary to law, or unsupported by substantial evidence.
14995: Military discharge and disability retirement: whether substantial evidence supported the Army Board for Correction of Military Records' finding that Melson was discharged from the Army Reserve in 2004 for non-disability reasons, so he was not entitled to a physical disability discharge or disability retirement benefits.
We determine that substantial evidence supports the Board's conclusion that Dr. Melson was discharged from the Army Reserve at his own request in 2004.
15008: Military disability retirement eligibility: whether Dillon, after his court-martial conviction, was ineligible for medical retirement under 10 U.S.C. §§ 1201-1202 and Army Regulation 635-40 ¶ 4-2, and whether disability processing continued until actual discharge.

In addition, Mr. Dillon has not shown error in the Claims Court's ruling that, on the facts alleged in his complaint, Mr. Dillon, once he was convicted, was ineligible for medical retirement in light of Army Regulation 635-40 ¶ 4-2 (2006)
15105: Military disability retirement: whether the Army Board for Correction of Military Records properly denied medical retirement with disability pay, including the claimed MEB referral failure and the effect of VA disability ratings; the court held the ABCMR decision was supported by substantial evidence and not contrary to law.
On this record, the ABCMR's decision is not arbitrary, capricious, unsupported by substantial evidence, or contrary to law.
15129: Military disability retirement claim: no evidence of a medical condition on active duty rendering him unfit, so failure to state a claim for disability retirement under 10 U.S.C. § 1201.

Because the record contains no evidence that Mr. Sanders suffered from a medical condition while on active duty that rendered him unfit to serve, we affirm the Claims Court's determination that he failed to state a claim for disability retirement.
15165: Military discharge and retirement: whether the Marine Corps breached the pretrial agreement and could proceed with separation based on the dismissed charges, and whether the BCNR properly rejected the claim.

The BCNR's conclusion that, despite his charges not being formally dismissed with prejudice, Mr. Carlborg received his benefit of the PTA—the withdrawal of his charges from the court-martial, is in accordance with law.
15166: Whether the Marine Corps was required to refer the servicemember to the Disability Evaluation System for PTSD-related unfitness.
we agree with the Claims Court that substantial evidence supports the BCNR's finding that Mr. Carlborg was not required to have been referred to the DES.
15167: Whether the Marine Corps violated regulations on the extension request, separation medical evaluation, and forwarding of the early retirement (TERA) request.
Mr. Carlborg was therefore not eligible for TERA because he was subject to both legal and administrative separation proceedings at the time he requested retirement.
